description: Renode's register DSL combinators. These are RULES, not emitter source code: the converter reads them from the database and knows nothing about any individual combinator. Adding support for a new one is a data change.

combinator_providers.note: The DSL does not live in one class, and naming only PeripheralRegisterExtensions named one of four. `DoubleWordRegisterExtensions` carries the REGISTER-level callbacks; `PeripheralRegister` carries the same field combinators as INSTANCE methods, which is how a register held in a local is extended; `PeripheralRegister<T>` carries what the register-level extensions forward to. Each of the three was skipped in silence, and one peripheral's whole register map was empty because of it.
combinator_providers.flag_note: Which combinators yield a one-bit handle, and therefore a `FlagId` rather than a `ValueId` in the generated Fields struct. Data, because it was the literal string `WithFlag` in the emitter: the instance form of the same combinator would have declared a ValueId for a one-bit field, which is a type error at the first site that emits both.
combinator_providers.leaf_note: `leaf_starts_with` says which of a provider's members are combinators. PeripheralRegister also declares UnderlyingValue, RecalculateFieldMask and fifty others; without it, widening the provider list turns every method call on a register into an unhandled combinator and buries the real ones.

callback_params.note: Every callback the DSL accepts, not the two the emitter happened to read. The corpus records changeCallback, readCallback and shadowReloadCallback as fully bound DelegateCreation arguments exactly as it records writeCallback; reading only two of them meant a changeCallback on bit 0 vanished while a writeCallback on bit 30 of the same register reported a gap. Detection is by the DSL's own naming convention (`suffix`), so a callback kind added upstream is inspected without a data change; the alias map only says which template slot each one fills, and a bound callback with no slot is a GAP.

soft_resettable.note: `softResettable: false` marks a field that a SOFT reset must leave alone. renode-regs' Bank has one reset, so the distinction has nowhere to land. Reported rather than dropped: a field that survives a soft reset in C# and does not here is a behavioural difference no trace of a hard reset can see.
soft_resettable.gap: `softResettable: false` -- the bank models one reset, so a field excluded from the soft reset is not modelled

unmodelled.note: changeCallback, readCallback and shadowReloadCallback have no slot in any rule, ON PURPOSE. Adding one means adding a hook to renode-regs, and a hook nothing calls is dead configuration -- the exact thing the write-callback asserts in renode-regs exist to reject. Of the 18 changeCallback sites in the cut, the two inside generated peripherals are both withheld for unrelated reasons (STM32_ADC's EnableADC reaches untranslated state; STM32_SYSCFG's is loop-replicated), so a runtime hook added today could not fire. They are reported instead, which is what makes the count visible and the work orderable.

rules.name: WITH_FLAG_BOUND_COMPUTED
rules.when: field and provider or field and writer
rules.note: `out` and the callbacks are independent in C#, and 22 call sites use both. The rule table had only `field` OR `provider or writer`, so the bound rule won and the callback fell off the end of the template with nothing reporting it -- the field kept its handle and silently lost its behaviour. `when` is read as a disjunction of conjunctions, which is why this can be stated at all.

negative.why: A one-bit combinator only. Routing a multi-bit field here would place a 1-bit field where the C# has N, and routing ANY bound-and-computed field to a reserved emitter would drop its writes -- Bank::write skips reserved fields, which is invisible to a trace.

rules.name: WITH_FLAG_COMPUTED
rules.note: A flag is a 1-bit value, so a computed flag routes through the same combinator rather than needing a parallel with_flag_cb.

rules.name: WITH_FLAG_ANONYMOUS
rules.note: A `WithFlag` that binds no `out` and carries no callback is still a STORED field -- the C# overload calls DefineFlagField, which appends to `registerFields`. It is anonymous, not tagged. This used to emit `.with_tagged_flag({pos})`, which is reserved, so `Bank::write` skipped it and the bit became write-ignored and read-as-zero. It also discarded `mode`: the tagged form hardcodes READ_WRITE, so five STM32F4_RTC `Read | WriteZeroToClear` flags and one write-only flag all lost their mode as well. `DefineFlagField` is the INSTANCE form of the same method -- literally the one the note above names -- so a call whose result nothing binds is the same anonymous stored field and takes the same arm; routing it anywhere reserved would reintroduce the defect through the door the instance combinators opened.

negative.why: those call PeripheralRegister.Tag, which appends to the separate `tags` list and stores NOTHING. Storing them would invent state the C# does not have -- the mirror of the bug this rule fixes, and equally invisible to a trace.
reserved bits exist so the register knows which bits are accounted for; giving them storage would make them readable.
every one of those pushes with reserved = true, which is what dropped the writes. An anonymous field must reach a storing combinator.

rules.name: WITH_VALUE_BOUND_COMPUTED
rules.when: field and provider or field and writer
rules.note: The multi-bit counterpart of WITH_FLAG_BOUND_COMPUTED; see its note.

negative.why: Singular only: the plural combinators define `count` consecutive fields, and emitting one would collapse a whole group to its first element. A bound-and-computed field must never reach a reserved emitter either -- Bank::write skips reserved fields, so the writes disappear and no trace can see it.

rules.name: WITH_VALUE_COMPUTED
rules.note: The callbacks become free fns emitted alongside; see peripheral_methods for why they cannot be closures.

rules.name: WITH_VALUE_ANONYMOUS
rules.note: The value-field counterpart of WITH_FLAG_ANONYMOUS, and the site the bug was found at: STM32F4_EXTI's `WithValueField(0, 32, name: "EMR")`, whose C# comment calls it a blank implementation kept for backwards compatibility. It is a read-write scratch register, and emitting `.with_tag(0, 32)` made it write-ignored and read-as-zero. The exti trace has no writes at all, so the oracle scored it 0 divergences throughout. `DefineValueField` / `DefineEnumField` are the INSTANCE forms the extension overloads forward to, so an unbound one is the same anonymous stored field and must not fall to a tag either.

negative.why: see WITH_FLAG_ANONYMOUS: a tag is a separate C# concept with no storage, and `name:` on a value field is documented as 'ignored ... treat it as a comment', so a name never makes a field a tag.
a reserved push is exactly the over-match; the field must store.

rules.name: WITH_FIELDS_COMPUTED
rules.note: The plural combinators bind a group of fields by `out IValueRegisterField[]` OR by callback -- `(idx, val) => mode[idx]`, with the group index as the first lambda parameter and no `out` anywhere. Only the `out` form had a rule, so the callback form matched nothing at all: five registers of one peripheral located, emitting nothing, and their already-generated callbacks left in the file as dead code. This is the plural counterpart of WITH_VALUE_COMPUTED and reads its callbacks the same way; the group index the C# lambda captures arrives as renode-regs' `group_index` parameter.

negative.why: A SINGULAR combinator routed here would be replicated `count` times over bits the C# never covers, and `count` is unbound for it -- silently plausible, structurally wrong. And a group carrying callbacks must never become reserved: Bank::write skips reserved fields, so every write to all `count` of them would vanish with the trace still green.

rules.name: WITH_TAGGED_FLAG
rules.note: A GENUINE tag: `WithTaggedFlag` calls PeripheralRegister.TaggedFlag, which appends to `tags`, a list the register's read and write paths never consult. Reserved is correct here and only here.

negative.shape: an anonymous WithFlag/WithValueField/WithEnumField, or the DefineFlagField/DefineValueField/DefineEnumField instance form of any of them -- no `out`, no assignment, no callbacks
negative.why: anonymity is not tagging. `name:` is documented in the C# as 'Ignored parameter, for convenience. Treat it as a comment.' -- the field is still created by DefineFlagField and still stores. Keying this rule on the absence of an `out` is what dropped 171 fields' writes.

negative.shape: an anonymous WithFlag/WithValueField/WithEnumField, or the DefineFlagField/DefineValueField/DefineEnumField instance form of any of them -- no `out`, no assignment, no callbacks
negative.why: see WITH_TAGGED_FLAG. Note the C# `WithIgnoredBits` is implemented as an anonymous `WithValueField` precisely BECAUSE it must cover the bits without tagging them -- so even a tag-like intent stores, and the discriminator is the combinator, never the argument list.

negative.shape: an anonymous WithFlag/WithValueField/WithEnumField, or the DefineFlagField/DefineValueField/DefineEnumField instance form of any of them -- no `out`, no assignment, no callbacks
negative.why: the third combinator that pushes reserved, and the one the invented `.with_reserved(9, 23)` came in as. A field with no handle is not a reserved field.

rules.name: REGISTER_WRITE_CALLBACK
rules.note: A callback on the REGISTER, not on a field: C# CallWriteHandlers fires it after every field's own write handler, on every write, whether or not anything changed. It resolves to DoubleWordRegisterExtensions rather than PeripheralRegisterExtensions, which is the only reason it was invisible -- the combinator table named one extension class. 18 sites. Its arguments are the register's whole old value and the whole written value, so the signature has no field index and is named separately from the field-level writeCallback of the same parameter name.
rules.deviation: The `old` argument is composed from the stored slots of the register's non-reserved fields. C# reads it from the register's single backing ulong, which also carries tag and reserved bits; renode-regs stores per field, so bits belonging to no field read back as zero here. No corpus callback reads the argument -- every one of the 18 discards both -- so the difference is recorded rather than paid for.
rules.cost_of_dropping_it: In STM32_UART both dropped callbacks call Update(), which recomputes the IRQ line, and they sit on registers whose flags are WriteZeroToClear. An ISR clearing RXNE/TC therefore never recomputed the line and it stayed asserted. A trace cannot observe an IRQ, so 33,164 replayed accesses at 100% said nothing about it.

negative.why: A write hook fires on every write. A READ callback fired there would run at the wrong time and a CHANGE callback would fire when nothing changed -- both plausible, both wrong, and neither observable in a trace. And this attaches to the REGISTER: a field-level combinator routed here would lose its bit position entirely.

rules.name: REGISTER_CALLBACK
rules.gap: register-level read/change callback: the bank has no hook to attach it to

negative.why: The write form IS emittable and has a hook. Folding it back in here would silently restore the defect this issue removed: STM32_UART's two Update() callbacks dropped, the IRQ line left asserted after an ISR cleared the flag, and a 33,164-access trace still at 100%.

rules.note: REACHABLE, and this rule previously was not: `combinator()` returned None for the whole of DoubleWordRegisterExtensions, so the gap text below had never appeared in any generated file. A rule whose code path cannot be reached reads exactly like a rule that correctly declines, which is why it survived. It now matches, and declines with a reason. Adding a read/change hook to renode-regs would be dead configuration today: neither kind occurs in a generated peripheral.

loop_replication.note: A register map written as a counted `for` loop. The layout walker read the SITE and never the loop around it, so four registers and sixteen fields were one register and one field whose position was an expression -- and because the expression is not a constant, the field was dropped and the register emitted empty.
loop_replication.why_unroll: The loop is deterministic and its bounds are literals, so every register it defines is known at CONVERSION time; there is nothing to defer to run time. Unrolling keeps the emitted shape identical to a hand-written map -- one `bank.define(..)` per register, constant bit positions, constant handle indices -- so nothing downstream needs a second code path. A Rust `for` around a moved builder would express the same registers and would additionally have to name the loop variable, size the handle array at run time, and be read against a C# loop to be believed. The DEVIATION is textual only: same registers, same fields, same order, no run-time loop.
loop_replication.limits: Only counted loops over a single variable with literal bounds and a unit step, and only arithmetic the evaluator folds. Anything else -- a bound read from a field, an index into a local array, a `foreach` -- yields no environment, and the site is REPORTED rather than emitted once and quietly wrong. STM32DMA's per-stream flag loop is in that second class: its offsets come from a local `int[]` literal, and it stays a reported gap.

register_forms.name: DEFINE_EXTENSION
register_forms.note: `Register.Status.Define(this, 0xC0, name: "USART_SR")` -- the offset is the enum member passed as the first argument, which Roslyn records as a constant.

register_forms.name: DICTIONARY_ADD
register_forms.note: `{(long)Registers.Mode, new DoubleWordRegister(this).With...}` -- a dictionary initialiser, which desugars to Dictionary.Add(key, value). Offset is the key; the combinator chain is inside the value.

expressions.name: FLAG_FIELD_READ
expressions.note: `someFlag.Value`. The symbol normalises to IRegisterField<T>.Value because call targets are keyed on OriginalDefinition, so flag-vs-value is distinguished by the RESULT TYPE, not the interface name.

expressions.name: IRQ_SET
expressions.note: `IRQ.Set(x)` drives the interrupt line. The GPIO object is not modelled yet, so this assigns the peripheral's own flag.

assignments.name: FLAG_FIELD_WRITE
assignments.note: `someFlag.Value = x`. Rust has no assignable property, and D2's handles are indices, so this is a bank call rather than an lvalue -- which is why assignment needs a PROJECT rule and not just the generic `{target} = {value}`.

callback_signatures.note: The DSL's callback types. `bank` and `state` are what the C# closure captured via `this`; `{state}` is the peripheral's generated State, because a callback must reach `st.receive_fifo` and a generic S cannot. The remaining SLOTS are named by the C# lambda itself -- `(idx, val) => ...` -- so the source's names are bound onto the trailing slots and the defaults below apply only where C# names nothing.

registerWriteCallback.note: REGISTER-level, not field-level. `WithWriteCallback((old, new) => ..)` takes the register's two values and no field index, so it cannot share the field-level shape even though C# names the parameter `writeCallback` in both. The rule names which signature applies; the parameter name alone cannot tell them apart.

peripheral_methods.note: EVERY peripheral method becomes a free fn over (bank, state) -- not only the ones that touch the bank. Inside a DSL callback you hold `&Bank<S>` and `&mut S`, which is the peripheral taken apart, so a method reached from a callback cannot have a `self`. Splitting methods by whether they touch registers would give two calling conventions and a classification that shifts as rules change; 49 of 296 methods in register-bearing types touch a field today, but which ones is not a stable property. Uniform is cheaper and needs no analysis.
peripheral_methods.why_handles_in_state: The field handles must be reachable from a free fn, so they live in S alongside the peripheral's data rather than in a sibling struct the callback cannot see.

unemitted_dependency.note: A callback body may call a peer method the converter cannot yet emit. Emitting the call anyway produces a file that does not compile and LOOKS finished; emitting a plausible stub is worse. So the callback is withheld, the combinator falls back to no callback, and the gap is reported by name. The register's layout is still correct -- only its behaviour is missing, and visibly so. The same applies when a body reaches a State field the converter could not type (GPIO's arrays of nested enums): the callback is withheld and the missing field named, rather than emitted against a struct that lacks it.

base_call.note: `base.Reset()` resolves to the BASE type's method, not the peripheral's. Rewriting it as a self-call produced `fn reset(...) { reset(bank, st); ... }` -- unbounded recursion that compiles cleanly and would only show up as a stack overflow at run time. Detected by comparing the callee's declaring type to the peripheral's own; the base class is not translated yet, so it is reported.
base_call.gap: calls base-class method `{name}` on `{type}`, which is not translated

withhold_on_unhandled.note: A method body containing a construct the converter cannot emit is withheld whole, exactly as a callback is. Emitting it produces markers in expression position (`f(a, /* DelegateCreation */, b)`) which do not parse, and anything that did parse would be a stub that looks finished. Withholding also cascades correctly: a callback depending on a withheld method is itself withheld, so the file stays consistent.

accessor_names.note: A property accessor arrives from Roslyn as `get_BaudRate`, but every CALL SITE is a PropertyReference that emits `baud_rate(bank, st)`. The prefix is stripped so the two agree; without it the file defines get_baud_rate and calls baud_rate.

withhold_on_gap_marker.note: A `/* GAP: ... */` marker is VALID RUST in statement position, so a method containing one compiles and runs -- wrongly. It produced a `while` loop whose increment had been replaced by the marker: an infinite loop that rustc accepts, the same failure class as the base.Reset() recursion. Any method whose body still carries a marker is therefore withheld, exactly as one with an unhandled construct is.

state_struct.note: The peripheral's non-register instance fields. The declared type decides: an IFlagRegisterField/IValueRegisterField/IEnumRegisterField is a HANDLE and already lives in `Fields`; anything else is real data and belongs in State. Derivable from the corpus, so State is generated rather than hand-declared -- which is what lets a callback reach `st.receive_fifo` in generated code.

also_state.note: State is not only `kind='field'`. A PROPERTY or EVENT can hold peripheral state too -- STM32_UART declares `IRQ` as a property and `CharReceived` as an event, and both were missing from a fields-only query.

type_map.note: Renode types with no BCL equivalent. `Core.GPIO` is an output line; the peripheral only ever sets its level, so `bool` carries it -- consistent with the IRQ_SET expression rule. `CancellationTokenSource` cancels a scheduled action, and under D3 (single-threaded) that is a shared flag, not a threading primitive: Cancel() sets it and the scheduled closure checks it before firing. This is a DEVIATION in mechanism with identical observable behaviour, recorded here rather than left to look like a faithful mapping.
type_map.register_value_note: RegisterValue is a thin wrapper over a CPU register's contents, declared outside the cut. It carries width metadata C# uses for formatting only; the VALUE is what the code reads and writes, so u64 is faithful. If width-dependent formatting is ever translated this becomes a newtype instead -- recorded so that is a decision rather than a surprise.

requires_storage.note: Only members that actually store go in State. `STM32_UART.BaudRate` computes from two register fields and holds nothing; emitting it as a field would invent storage the C# does not have -- the same error class as the invented `.with_reserved(9, 23)`. Derived from member.has_storage, so it is not a hand-maintained skip list.

elided.note: Base-class members that renode-regs' Bank ALREADY IS. `RegistersCollection` and `mapper` are the register collection and its offset mapping; the Rust peripheral receives them as the `bank` parameter, so carrying them in State too would model the same thing twice. Elided with a reason rather than reported as gaps, which would imply work that does not exist. `machine` and `sysbus` are NOT elided -- they are real unmodelled infrastructure and stay visible.

callback_naming.note: Deterministic from the register name and bit position -- both content, never emission order, so output stays byte-identical at -j1 and -j31.
callback_naming.register_note: A register-level callback has no bit position, and formatting None into the name gave `status_None_writer` -- a name that reads like a bug and is not derived from anything.

logging.note: Renode's `this.Log(LogLevel.X, format, args...)`. A STATIC extension on IEmulationElement, so argument 0 is the peripheral and argument 1 the level -- binding from the front would log at level `self`. Kept out of `expressions` because it needs the level argument decoded, which a flat template cannot express.

unwrap_format.note: C# passes an interpolated string as the message, which emits as format!(..). The log macros take format arguments THEMSELVES, so a nested format! is both redundant and a compile error -- the macro requires a string literal. The wrapper is unwrapped so the literal and its arguments pass straight through.

enums.note: C# enums nested in the peripheral are generated alongside it. Discriminants are emitted EXPLICITLY from the corpus, never renumbered by declaration order: the values are written into registers, so a renumbering is a silent hardware change the oracle would catch late.
enums.default_note: Default is the LOWEST discriminant, matching C#, where an enum field's default is 0 rather than its first declared member.

skip_offset_enum.note: The register-offset enum is already emitted as `mod reg`, so emitting it again as a Rust enum duplicates it. Identified by CONTENT -- its members match the emitted offsets -- rather than by being called `Register` or `Registers`, which differs per peripheral and would be a name check pretending to be a rule.

enums.reference_note: Emitted as the DISCRIMINANT. A register stores the numeric value, and the bank reads and writes u64, so an enum-typed field compares against its discriminant -- which is what the hardware holds. Recorded as a representation deviation: C# keeps the enum type through `.Value`, Rust keeps the number.

from_u64.note: C# casts a register value straight to the enum: `(OutputSpeed)val`. Rust has no such cast, so each generated enum gets a from_u64. DEVIATION: C# keeps an out-of-range discriminant (`(OutputSpeed)7` stays 7), which Rust cannot represent, so an unmatched value falls back to the default. In practice the field width bounds the value -- a 2-bit field over a 4-member enum is total -- but the fallback is recorded rather than assumed unreachable.

typed_callback_param.note: WithEnumFields gives C# a STRONGLY TYPED callback -- `(idx, val)` where val is already the enum, with no cast node anywhere. The Rust callback signature is u64, so the conversion belongs at the parameter's uses inside the body. Scoped to lambda slots: a peripheral method that genuinely takes an enum parameter declares it as the enum and must not be wrapped.

aliases.note: C# permits two names for one discriminant (`Default = 0, Receive = 0`); Rust forbids it -- E0081, discriminant assigned more than once. The first name by declaration order becomes the VARIANT and the rest become associated consts pointing at it, which preserves both names and both spellings at use sites without inventing a value.

inheritance.note: Rust has no inheritance, so a peripheral's base class is FLATTENED into it: base fields join State, base methods are emitted as free fns over the same (bank, st). This is the object-model deviation D1 applied to peripherals -- recorded here because the alternative, a trait, cannot carry the base's FIELDS, which is what the derived code actually reaches for.
inheritance.qualified_note: When the derived type overrides a base method, both flatten to the same name. `base.Reset()` therefore calls the base's version under a name qualified by its declaring type -- unambiguous at any depth, and derived from the corpus rather than a hand-kept table.
inheritance.skip_when_external: A base outside the corpus cut (BaseGPIOPort) cannot be flattened; the derived members that need it are withheld and the gap names the type.

register_collection.note: The C# RegistersCollection IS renode-regs' Bank -- it was elided from State for that reason, so its uses must resolve to `bank` rather than to a fabricated accessor. The bank threads `&mut S` through read/write because callbacks need the peripheral's state, which is why the argument lists differ from C#. Matched on BaseRegisterCollection, the generic DECLARATION Roslyn resolves calls to -- the concrete DoubleWordRegisterCollection never appears at a call site, because targets are keyed on OriginalDefinition.

members.Read: bank.read({arg0} as u64, st).unwrap_or(0) as u32
members.Write: bank.write({arg0} as u64, {arg1} as u64, st)

register_collection.cast_note: C# types the bus offset as `long` and the value as `uint`; the bank uses u64 for both, so the casts are at the boundary. Faithful: the C# signature is what the bus calls, and the width is not narrowed.

object_graph.note: D1: every C# reference-typed field becomes Rc<RefCell<T>>, Option<...> where C# permits null. Renode's graph is cyclic by construction -- the machine owns peripherals and peripherals hold IMachine back-references -- so cycles are unavoidable and LEAKING them is correct: the machine is built once and lives for the process, which then exits.
object_graph.blocked_on: An INTERFACE-typed field needs the trait to exist. Generating it is issue #41's recommendation and carries a real decision this rule does not make: IMachine declares 112 members and the corpus calls 6. A full trait is faithful but mostly untranslatable; a used-subset trait compiles but is not IMachine, and would quietly redefine what the type means. Recorded here so the field mapping is settled while the trait question stays visible.
object_graph.risk: D1 records the known risk: RefCell panics on re-entrant borrow, and the real exposure is peripheral -> sysbus -> peripheral. A panic there is NOT necessarily a C# bug -- it can be re-entrancy C# tolerates. PLAN.md calls this the highest-risk item and wants a borrow discipline decided in Phase 0.

interface_traits_moved: The translatability-subset trait rule lived here and is SUPERSEDED. Issue #60 took the opposite decision -- generate the full interface, map the blocked member types first -- because membership that depends on the converter's maturity is a shape nothing downstream can rely on. The rule is now `interface_traits` in csharp_core.json, where it belongs: a C# interface becoming a Rust trait is a fact about the two LANGUAGES and mentions nothing about this corpus. The generated traits and the per-member blockers are docs/status/interfaces.md.

sub_blocks.note: A child class that defines registers into its PARENT's collection, instantiated N times. `(Registers.StreamConfiguration + id * StreamStep).Define(parent)` -- one flat register map, not a bank per child, so the translation is a loop in the parent's define_registers and NOT an offset-routing dispatch.
sub_blocks.detected_by: the child holds a back-reference field typed as the parent, AND one of its own methods yields registers when the register forms are run over it. Both read from the corpus; neither is a name match, so the rule does not fit one corpus.
sub_blocks.not_this: An array of child objects with no register block of their own. Five of the six array-of-class fields in the cut are that, and they are an ordinary Vec.
sub_blocks.child_fn: pub fn define_registers(bank: &mut Bank<super::State>, f: &mut Fields, st: &State) {{
sub_blocks.parent_field:
/// One set of handles per `{child}`; the register map is the parent's.
    pub {field}: Vec<{module}::Fields>,
sub_blocks.gap_count: sub-block `{field}`: the constructor does not give a constant instance count, so the register map cannot be replicated
sub_blocks.gap_identity: sub-block `{field}`: the child takes no single instance index alongside its back-reference, so its registers cannot be placed
